answer: State rent makes bulk farming unaffordable by charging upkeep, not just entry. Each identity anchors its work history in the public trellis and pays 20 opal per epoch; unpaid identities are pruned. The k-th fake pays the k-th rent stream: 1,000 fakes burn 20,000 opal every epoch, while one honest agent pays 20 and keeps full weight. History rental fails because rented records are key-bound and checked against fresh work.
